elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: New clause: "The license granted under section 2(a) extends to Client's affiliates upon written notice to TrueLink". "Client" is defined as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone, so this is additive rather than duplicative.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither section 2(a) nor the inserted clause mentions contractors, subcontractors, agents or service providers acting on Client's behalf; the grant runs to Client and its affiliates only.
Section 2(c) retains "The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated in accordance with section 12"; no perpetual term for any paid-up licence is stated.

No "irrevocable" language appears in the grant or the inserted clause; the licence remains co-terminous with the Agreement. (No at-will revocation right for TrueLink is expressed either, but the affirmative irrevocability element is absent.)

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Section 2(c) ties licence duration to any termination "in accordance with section 12" without limiting the trigger to uncured material breach; no operative language confines licence loss to that ground.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "notwithstanding section 15, Client may transfer the license to its successor in a merger or acquisition" — a Client-only transfer right that overrides the section 15 consent bar.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause extends the section 2(a) licence to "Client's affiliates upon written notice to TrueLink"; written-notice trigger is express and the affiliate grant carries use through those affiliates' authorized personnel without a separate personnel edit, and no retained sentence contradicts it.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause expressly permits Client to "transfer the license to its successor in a merger or acquisition", with "notwithstanding section 15" resolving the retained consent requirement; section 15 is otherwise untouched so TrueLink gains no new assignment exception.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: both fallback elements are met in operative language (affiliate extension on written notice; Client-only transfer to an M&A successor), so the redline is acceptable at the fallback and no further edit is required for compliance.

Preferred level remains incomplete. To reach preferred the drafter would need, in operative language: (i) add "and contractors acting on Client's behalf" to the section 2(a) grant; (ii) state that any paid-up licence is perpetual and irrevocable; and (iii) amend section 2(c) so the licence terminates only on Client's uncured material breach rather than on any section 12 termination.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion, no deletions, no expansion of TrueLink's section 15 assignment rights, no survival tails, expense language, procedures or other model-language extras, and no duplication (Client is defined as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone, so affiliate coverage was genuinely absent).

Intent preserved: section 2(a) (including the favourable non-exclusivity and free-to-use-alternatives sentence), section 2(c) term, section 2(d) ownership and section 15 all survive intact; the "notwithstanding section 15" carve-out prevents a contradictory retained sentence and leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in substance): the inserted paragraph is rendered as "Affiliates and Transfer." without the "e." numbering referenced in the comment; add the subsection label for clean execution.
